# s233 — Name the tracking-file read ban in the skill description

An agent sees the read ban before the slicer skill body loads, in every project that installs the skill.

**Findings:** session 2026-10-07: an agent read .slicer/slices/s231.json while the slicer skill was still loading; the always-visible skill description does not carry the read ban · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** a hook that blocks tool reads, changes to the skill body or the instructions text, or the per-project AGENTS.md wording.

## Why

The skill's frontmatter `description` is the only slicer text an agent host shows before the skill loads. It says when to use the skill, but not that tracking files are off limits. The ban is the first line of the body. On 2026-10-07 an agent sent a read of `.slicer/slices/s231.json` in the same batch as the skill load, so the body arrived after the read. `git status` had listed the path, which made it look like the obvious file to open.

## Files

- `src/slicer/ai.py`: `SKILL_DESCRIPTION`.
- `skills/slicer/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/slicer/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/slicer/SKILL.md`: regenerated with `slicer ai skill`.
- `tests/test_ai.py`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`.

## Failing tests

- The frontmatter description in `ai.skill_text()` says to read roadmap state through slicer commands and not to open `.slicer/` tracking files.
- The description stays one line, contains no colon followed by a space or other character that breaks YAML frontmatter, and stays under 1024 characters.
- The checked-in SKILL.md copies stay byte-equal to `ai.skill_text()`.

## Implement

Extend `SKILL_DESCRIPTION` with one sentence after the trigger list, for example: "Read and change roadmap state only through slicer commands, never by opening .slicer/ files." Keep the trigger wording first so matching does not change. Regenerate the three checked-in copies and update any test that pins the old string.
